_doc: Source strings (English) for the free tools pages – docs/SEO-TOOLS.md. Keep {placeholders} and <b>/<i> tags. Exam names (IELTS, TOEIC, CEFR, Part 5) and Lexkite stay untranslated.

test.title: Free English Level Test (CEFR A1–C2) – 15 minutes, instant result
test.desc: Find your English level from A1 to C2 in about 15 minutes. Adaptive questions, instant CEFR result with IELTS and TOEIC equivalents and a personal study plan. Free, no sign-up.
test.h1: Free English level test: find your CEFR level (A1–C2)
test.lead: Answer about 30 grammar, vocabulary and reading questions. The test adapts to you: right answers bring harder questions, wrong answers easier ones. In about 15 minutes you get your estimated CEFR level, rough IELTS and TOEIC equivalents and a step-by-step plan.
test.idkHint: Not sure? Choose "I don't know" instead of guessing – your result will be more accurate.
test.examsNote: Approximate, based on the published CEFR alignments of Cambridge English (IELTS) and ETS (TOEIC Listening & Reading). Only an official exam gives an official score.
test.noJs: This test needs JavaScript. Please enable it, or open the Lexkite app.
test.loadErr: The questions could not load. Check your connection and try again.
how: Every question has a difficulty from A1 to C2. After each answer the test re-estimates your level and picks the most informative next question, the same idea used by computer-adaptive exams.
Questions mix grammar, vocabulary and short reading texts. All questions were written by the Lexkite team for this test; none are copied from official exams.
The test stops when your level is clear (usually after 25–32 questions), so most people finish in 12–18 minutes.
test.levelsLead: The Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) describes language ability on six levels. Open a level to see what it means and how to reach the next one.
test.honest: A short adaptive test gives a good estimate, not a certificate. Your result shows a likely range as well as a single level. Speaking and writing are not tested here; listening and speaking practice in the app fills that gap.
test.privacy: The test runs entirely in your browser. Your answers are not sent anywhere and no account is needed.
test.otherTool: Preparing for TOEIC? Try the free Part 5 practice quiz.

A1.name: Beginner
A1.desc: You can understand and use very common everyday expressions and simple phrases.
can: Introduce yourself and ask simple personal questions
Understand very slow, clear speech about familiar things
Read short notices, menus and forms
Write a short note with basic personal information

A2.name: Elementary
A2.desc: You can handle simple, routine tasks and talk about your background and immediate needs.
can: Shop, order food and ask for directions
Understand the main point of short, clear announcements
Read short personal emails and simple instructions
Write a short message about everyday plans

B1.name: Intermediate
B1.desc: You can deal with most everyday situations and talk about experiences, plans and opinions in simple connected sentences.
can: Handle most situations while travelling
Follow the main points of clear talk on familiar topics
Read straightforward articles and work emails
Write a simple connected text and give reasons for an opinion

B2.name: Upper intermediate
B2.desc: You can communicate with native speakers fluently enough that neither side finds it a strain, and understand the main ideas of complex texts.
can: Take an active part in meetings and discussions
Understand most TV news and films in standard English
Read articles where writers take a particular point of view
Write a clear, detailed essay arguing for or against an idea

C1.name: Advanced
C1.desc: You can use English flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes.
can: Express ideas fluently without obviously searching for words
Understand long, complex speech even when it is not clearly structured
Read long technical or literary texts and notice style
Write well-structured reports with precise vocabulary

C2.name: Proficient
C2.desc: You can understand almost everything you hear or read and express yourself very fluently and precisely.
can: Follow any kind of spoken English, even at fast native speed
Read abstract, complex or very idiomatic texts with ease
Express fine shades of meaning in complex situations
Write complex reports, reviews and summaries in an appropriate style

toeic.title: TOEIC Part 5 practice test online – free, with explanations
toeic.desc: Free TOEIC Reading Part 5 (Incomplete Sentences) practice: {n} original questions, instant scoring and a clear explanation for every answer. No sign-up.
toeic.lead: Each set has 10 questions written in the style of TOEIC Reading Part 5. Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence, then read the explanation. Aim for about 20 seconds per question, as in the real test.
toeic.tipsH: How to answer Part 5 questions fast
tips: Look at the four choices first. If they are forms of the same word (tidy, tidily, tidiness), it is a word-form question: check the word before and after the blank.
If the choices are different verb forms, find a time clue such as next spring, since 2019 or by the time.
If the choices are four different words with similar meanings, read the whole sentence and look for the collocation (meet a deadline, place an order).
toeic.about: All questions are original and written by the Lexkite team in the style of the TOEIC Listening and Reading test. TOEIC is a registered trademark of ETS; this practice is not endorsed by ETS.
